result.note: Tests the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool's first sovereign-backed P&I policy and India's diplomatic and advisory response to attacks on ships with Indian crew in July 2026.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool as of July 2026:
items: New India Assurance issued the first sovereign-backed Protection and Indemnity policy under the pool to Shipping Corporation of India.
The first Protection and Indemnity policy covers third-party liabilities of up to USD 500 million.
The pool has written over 1,600 war-risk policies since May 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The policy issued to Shipping Corporation of India covers third-party liabilities up to USD 1.5 billion, not USD 500 million. The pool has written 1,608 war-risk policies since May, with premiums down 35 to 40% from the conflict peak, as India swaps dependence on foreign insurers for its own balance sheet.
questions.source: New India Assurance issued the first sovereign-backed Protection and Indemnity policy under the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool to Shipping Corporation of India, covering third-party liabilities up to USD 1.5 billion.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's response to attacks on merchant ships carrying Indian seafarers in July 2026:
items: India summoned Ukraine's ambassador over the attack on MV Omorfi, which killed an Indian national.
India's July 26 advisory on Black Sea assignments did not impose a deployment ban of the kind imposed on Hormuz.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both are correct. India summoned Ukraine's ambassador over MV Omorfi a week after summoning Russia's chargé over four deaths aboard MV Golden Leo, and the July 26 advisory left seafarers to weigh Black Sea assignments themselves rather than banning deployment.
questions.source: A July 26 advisory told seafarers to weigh Black Sea assignments themselves, with no deployment ban of the kind imposed on Hormuz.
